John Doe is an American researcher at the University of Michigan and the father of a young daughter, Elena. The latter has just finished high school and is wondering about her career path, but she's particularly interested in careers in the health sector. So she enlists her father's help to sort things out. John is a scientist, so it's only natural that he should justify any decision on the basis of concrete statistics. 

To do this, he collects data on healthcare occupations in the USA. He then looks for a list of occupations with the highest employment rates in the U.S.

```{r}
## Load data
national <- read_excel("national_M2021_dl.xlsx") %>% clean_names()
```


```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
national %>% 
  distinct(occ_title, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(str_detect(occ_code,"29-|31-"),!(tot_emp=="**"), !(a_mean %in% c("*","#"))) %>%
  mutate(
    a_mean=as.numeric(a_mean),
    tot_emp=as.numeric(tot_emp)
  )%>%
  arrange(desc(tot_emp)) %>%
  mutate(prop=round(tot_emp*100/sum(tot_emp))) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=prop, y=reorder(occ_title,prop)))+
  geom_col()+
  geom_text(aes(label=paste(prop,"%")), hjust=1.2, size=6, color="white") +
  labs(title="Occupations with the most estimated employment",
       subtitle="Top 5 by proportion of estimated employment in 2021",
       y="Occupations",
       x=NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  # remove legend
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        text = element_text("Poppins", size=18),
        # remove tick marks
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        # remove major horizontal grids
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        # remove both minor grids
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

John then asks what the average annual salary for these occupations would be.

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
national %>% 
  distinct(occ_title, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(mean_wage=mean(as.numeric(a_mean), na.rm = TRUE))%>%
  filter(str_detect(occ_code,"29-|31-"),!(tot_emp=="**"), !(a_mean %in% c("*","#"))) %>%
  mutate(
    a_mean=as.numeric(a_mean),
    tot_emp=as.numeric(tot_emp)
  )%>%
  arrange(desc(tot_emp)) %>%
  mutate(prop=round(tot_emp*100/sum(tot_emp)),
         highlight=as.numeric(a_mean)>mean_wage) %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=reorder(occ_title,prop), y=as.numeric(a_mean), fill=highlight))+
  geom_col()+
  geom_text(aes(label=paste(as.numeric(a_mean), "$")), hjust=1.2, size=6, color="white", face=rep(c("bold")))+
  annotate("segment", x=0.5, xend=5.7, y=67382.66, yend = 67382.66, color="darkred", linewidth=1.5)+
  annotate("segment", y = 75000, yend = 68383, x = 1.5, xend = 1.5,
           size = 1.5, arrow = arrow(length = unit(.25,"cm")))+
  annotate( "text", y=72000, x=1.5, label="Mean Wage in U.S.",hjust=-0.2, size=5)+
  coord_flip()+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gray30", "darkgreen")) +
  labs(title="Annual Wage in Health Occupations",
       subtitle="Mean annual wage in top 5 Health Occupations",
       x="Occupations",
       y=NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  # remove legend
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        text = element_text("Poppins", size=18),
        # remove legend
        legend.position = "none",
        # remove tick marks
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        # remove both minor grids
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
